# Results — Study 912 (Gold + Trend) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The rule: hold **GLD** (gold)
only when its price is above its **200-day** simple moving average; otherwise sit in
**BIL** (1-3 month T-bills, the cash leg). Binary, no shorting, one-day rebalance lag,
5 bps one-way cost. Every leg is measured **excess-of-cash** (minus the BIL total-return
leg) so the Sharpe race is apples-to-apples. Daily total-return closes (`yfinance`,
`auto_adjust=True`). Common GLD∩BIL window 2007-05-30 → 2026-06-30 (BIL inception gates
the tradable cash leg). As-of **2026-06-30** (the partial current month is dropped) —
data stamp as-of 2026-06-30.*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| GLD (gold), BIL (cash) | 2007-05-30 → 2026-06-30 | 4,802 | Fingerprint `3ea3fb6649e8` |

Cross-checks: IAU (second gold ETF), SPY / TLT (diversification benchmarks) are cached too.

## The three arms — buy-and-hold gold vs 200-day trend vs random control

All three are reported **excess-of-cash**. The random control holds cash on random days at
the *same* in-market frequency (63.0%) as the trend rule — it isolates *timing* from mere
*exposure reduction*. Drawdowns are the *absolute* (lived) max drawdown.

| Arm | Excess Sharpe | CAGR | Vol | Max drawdown | HAC *t* (mean) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Buy-and-hold gold** | **+0.520** | +8.08% | 18.1% | **−45.6%** | +2.37 |
| **200-day trend overlay** | **+0.332** | +3.78% | 14.2% | **−35.3%** | +1.52 |
| Random control (null) | +0.142 | +1.02% | 14.2% | −55.3% | +0.64 |

- **Excess-Sharpe advantage (trend − buy-and-hold): −0.188** — the trend overlay has a
  *lower* risk-adjusted return than simply holding gold. The HAC *t* on the daily return
  difference is **−1.83** (wrong sign vs the claim, and short of |*t*| = 2).
- **Trend does beat the random control** (+0.190 excess-Sharpe, *t* = +0.96; DD −35.3% vs
  −55.3%) — so the overlay *is* doing genuine timing, not just cutting exposure. That
  genuine timing still under-performs buy-and-hold, because gold's biggest up-moves come
  in sharp V-recoveries off the lows that a 200-day filter re-enters too late.
- **Drawdown:** the overlay cuts the worst drawdown from −45.6% to −35.3% (+10.3 pp) — real
  but modest, and (see the era cut) *not* present in the recent era.

## Bootstrap Sharpe CIs (excess-of-cash, 2,000 draws, 21-day blocks)

| Arm | Excess Sharpe | 95% CI | share < 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Buy-and-hold gold | +0.520 | [+0.093, +0.943] | 0.9% |
| Trend overlay | +0.332 | [−0.105, +0.753] | 5.9% |

The trend overlay's Sharpe CI **includes zero** and sits *below* buy-and-hold's; the
overlay does not improve the risk-adjusted return with any confidence.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2016-01-01)

| Era | n | BH exSharpe | Trend exSharpe | Advantage (*t*) | BH DD → Trend DD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2007–2015 | 2,164 | +0.34 | +0.06 | **−0.28** (*t* = −1.17) | −45.6% → −35.3% |
| 2016–2026 | 2,636 | +0.70 | +0.50 | **−0.20** (*t* = −1.70) | −26.2% → **−30.2%** |

The advantage is **negative in both halves**. The entire drawdown benefit comes from the
early era (ducking the 2013 gold crash); in the recent era the overlay's drawdown is
actually *deeper* than buy-and-hold's — the drawdown-management story is **not era-robust**.

## Calendar-year fingerprint (why it lags)

The overlay's cost is visible year by year: it missed the +27% 2007 melt-up (out on the
warmup), took −24.8% in 2008 (whipsawed half-in through the crash), ducked the −28% 2013
crash cleanly (+8% in gold that year → −4.4%), but then gave back the edge whipsawing in
2014, 2017, 2021 and 2022. It fully captured the +64% 2025 gold run (both legs long).

## Cost sensitivity

The rule is low-turnover (~150 switches over 19 years, ~8/yr), so costs are not what kills
it — the edge is negative before any cost:

| One-way cost | Trend exSharpe | Advantage (*t*) | Max DD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | +0.360 | −0.160 (*t* = −1.68) | −33.8% |
| 5 bps | +0.332 | −0.188 (*t* = −1.83) | −35.3% |
| 25 bps | +0.222 | −0.299 (*t* = −2.39) | −43.5% |

## Cross-checks

- **IAU** (second gold ETF): advantage **−0.183** (*t* = −1.82), DD −45.1% → −35.3% — the
  same picture on an independent gold tape (not a GLD idiosyncrasy).
- **Synthetic control** (machinery proof only, never supports the stamp): on a *planted*
  persistent dead-decade grind the overlay cuts drawdown by +23.4 pp and lifts the excess
  Sharpe by +0.14; on the flat-vol null the excess-Sharpe advantage is centred at 0
  (mean −0.05, sd 0.13, fires on 0/8 seeds). The detector is unbiased — the real-tape
  under-performance is a property of the *gold tape*, not a broken harness.

## Verdict

- **Signal — None.** The marquee claim — that a 200-day trend filter turns gold into a
  *better-Sharpe* drawdown-managed diversifier — does **not** hold on the real tape. The
  excess-of-cash Sharpe advantage is **−0.188** with the **wrong sign** (HAC *t* = −1.83);
  the bootstrap CI for the overlay's Sharpe [−0.11, +0.75] includes zero and sits below
  buy-and-hold's [+0.09, +0.94]; and the advantage is negative in **both** sub-eras. The
  fallback drawdown benefit (+10 pp overall) is real but modest and **not era-robust** — it
  reverses in 2016–2026, where the overlay's drawdown is *deeper* than buy-and-hold's. The
  overlay does beat a random control (genuine timing), but genuine timing that
  under-performs the asset it times is not the claimed edge.
- **Tradability — Mirage.** There is no positive net edge to bank: the advantage is
  negative gross and grows more negative with cost (−0.30 at 25 bps). The apparent
  "drawdown insurance" is paid for with ~4.3 pp/yr of CAGR (8.08% → 3.78%) and a −0.19
  Sharpe give-up, for a worst-case-loss reduction that is absent in the recent decade. A
  gold holder is better served holding gold (and sizing it) than trend-timing it.
- **Risk reduction or alpha?** Neither, robustly. It is a volatility *reducer* (vol 18.1%
  → 14.2%) that reduces return more than risk on this tape — the opposite of the Sharpe
  improvement the rule promises.
